title: Learning Loop Resolver Attribution vs Mathematical Day Lens Selection
status: DECIDED — resolver credit stays on the signal-first display leader
decision: Do not retarget dominant_expert_for_learning onto selection_weights. Day Lens (1.05 / 0.90 / 1.08 / 1.05, then normalized) remains the day-score tilt inside score_subnet_for_day. The published thesis is leading_expert_for_pick: classifiable signals win, otherwise the learned-weight blend, with alphabetical-later tie-break. record_pick_prediction stores that expert. resolve_expert_attribution keeps an already-stamped expert. New credits therefore match the badge and the historical rows.
why_not_selection_weights: Crediting the Day Lens argmax would nudge a different expert from the one shown on the pick, and it would make unstamped replay rows use a second credit definition. The mismatch is provenance, not a scoring defect.
rule: dominant_expert_for_learning stays an alias of leading_expert_for_pick. No Day Lens factor change.
observation: dominant_expert_for_learning() returns leading_expert_for_pick(), the signal-first display leader. Day selection uses selection_weights (Day Lens 1.05 / 0.90 / 1.08 / 1.05, then normalized) inside score_subnet_for_day. A momentum_shift signal can credit hype in the resolver while Day Lens selected dark_horse. That credit is what the learning loop trains. The decision is to keep that split.
